life Aim, imagery and effects · v7
v7 · Meet you where you are. Show you where you're going.

Images that know how you feel, and a glimpse of the life you're building.

Three new art directions, each given a job. A picture system that starts where your mood is and, as you make good decisions, starts showing you the life in your Chief Aim. The Aim itself, with the teaching behind it. And the Apple-native effects that make it feel like it belongs on an iPhone.

01 · Four art directions

Not one look. Four, each with a job.

Instead of picking a single style, each direction does a different job in the app. Bright daylight for the brand, colour fields for tools, glimpses for growth, and v6's quiet set for low moods and night.

02 · Mood-adaptive imagery

It starts where you are, then shows you where you could be.

Today's picture follows your Pulse check-in, so a drained morning gets something soft, not a sunny beach. As you clear missions and move toward your Aim, glimpses start to appear: images of the specific life you wrote down. They're earned, never handed out.

03 · Chief Aim

One clear aim, written down, read every day.

This is the idea of a definite major aim, made popular by Napoleon Hill: know exactly what you want, by when, what you'll give for it, and the plan, then keep it in front of you daily. In life, the Aim sits above everything: Aim (years) → this month's gambit → today's moves. The teaching lives in Learn.

04 · Apple-native effects

The slick stuff, and where it comes from.

All of these are real libraries for your Expo version (SDK 58), checked on npm today. The demos below are web approximations; on the phone they're Apple's own rendering.

05 · What else to bring in

The rest of a real, shippable app.

Ranked by when you need it. Now means before the first TestFlight. Later means before the App Store.
